currentUse: No surviving congregation, worship site, or successor has been established for Waterbury's historical All Saints Lithuanian independent/national Catholic effort. No church address, property record, building, or exact institutional end has yet been identified.
summary: Waterbury's Visų Šventųjų (All Saints) belongs to the history of the Lithuanian National Catholic movement, not to the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hartford. A 2015 scholarly study dates the attempt to organize the parish to November 1902, when conflict had developed between the pastor and parishioners of Waterbury's Roman Catholic St. Joseph Lithuanian parish. The study identifies Rev. Vincas R. Dilionis as the organizer and concludes that the independent parish did not take root. A 1984 Draugas retrospective preserves the All Saints name and also associates the former seminarian Rusikas with the Waterbury effort, creating a limited source disagreement about who participated. The historical record establishes a distinct Lithuanian independent church effort, but not a lasting congregation, formal Polish National Catholic Church affiliation, church address, property, building, or exact end date. Today's Roman Catholic All Saints/Todos los Santos Parish in Waterbury was created in 2017 and is a different institution.

historicalNarrative.text: All Saints emerged from a dispute inside Waterbury's established Lithuanian Roman Catholic community. A scholarly history of the Lithuanian National Catholic Church dates the organizing attempt to November 1902, when tension had developed between Rev. Petras Siaurusaitis and parishioners of St. Joseph, Waterbury's Roman Catholic Lithuanian parish. The organizer was Rev. Vincas R. Dilionis, also known in the sources as Vincas Petraitis.

sources.locator: Ilona Strumickienė, “Lietuvių tautinė katalikų bažnyčia Amerikoje,” Oikos 2015 Nr. 1 (19), printed p. 58 (PDF p. 28): November 1902 Waterbury attempt, St. Joseph dispute, and Vincas R. Dilionis

historicalNarrative.text: The proposed parish was called Visų Šventųjų—All Saints—and was meant to be independent of Roman Catholic episcopal control. In this period, Lithuanian sources used several overlapping terms for such communities, including national, independent, and “neprigulminga.” They reflected demands that parishioners govern property and parish affairs themselves. The label does not make this record part of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hartford, and the surviving evidence does not establish a formal, lasting affiliation with the Polish National Catholic Church.

historicalNarrative.text: The sources agree on Dilionis and on the All Saints identity, but differ about Rusikas. The 1984 Draugas retrospective says Dilionis and the former seminarian Rusikas went to Waterbury and began an independent All Saints church for Lithuanians. The later scholarly reconstruction names Dilionis alone in Waterbury and places Rusikas with him in the unsuccessful Baltimore effort of 1903. Until a contemporary Waterbury source is found, Rusikas's role in the 1902 attempt remains unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: The Waterbury initiative was brief. The 2015 study concludes that the independent parish did not take root, while the Cleveland State University history describes the first Lithuanian National Catholic parishes—including Waterbury—as short-lived. Neither source supplies a closure decree or end date. No address, deed, dedicated church building, cemetery, sacramental-record repository, or later successor has been established, so the physical history must remain open rather than being assigned a building outcome.

historicalNarrative.text: This historical All Saints must also be kept separate from two present-day records. Waterbury's Roman Catholic St. Joseph was the city's long-lived Lithuanian parish; it is not this independent effort. The current All Saints/Todos los Santos Parish, whose official site identifies it as a multicultural Roman Catholic parish centered at the Shrine of Saint Anne, was formed under the Archdiocese of Hartford in 2017 and does not continue the 1902 Lithuanian National Catholic initiative. The current Eastern Diocese directory of the Polish National Catholic Church lists no Waterbury parish, but that present-day absence by itself cannot establish when the historical effort ended.

developments.headline: All Saints independent parish attempted in Waterbury
developments.detail: Ilona Strumickienė's scholarly reconstruction dates the attempt to November 1902. Rev. Vincas R. Dilionis sought to organize Visų Šventųjų (All Saints) amid tension between Rev. Petras Siaurusaitis and parishioners of Waterbury's Roman Catholic St. Joseph Lithuanian parish. The study concludes that the new parish did not take root.

developments.headline: Draugas retrospective preserves the All Saints name
developments.detail: The historical survey names an independent All Saints church for Lithuanians in Waterbury and associates both Dilionis and Rusikas with it. A later scholarly study places Rusikas in the 1903 Baltimore attempt instead, so his Waterbury role remains unresolved.

developments.headline: Modern directory review finds no surviving Waterbury successor
developments.detail: The Eastern Diocese PNCC directory lists no Waterbury parish. The active All Saints/Todos los Santos Parish in Waterbury identifies itself as Roman Catholic and is a separate institution created in the twenty-first century. These findings distinguish the identities but do not supply an end date or building history for the 1902 effort.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The identity, All Saints name, Waterbury location, 1902 organizing date, and Vincas R. Dilionis are supported. Two refinements are necessary. First, the strongest scholarly reconstruction describes the November 1902 event as an attempted parish that did not take root, rather than a durable congregation with a documented institutional life. Second, the 1984 Draugas retrospective associates the former seminarian Rusikas with Dilionis in Waterbury, while Ilona Strumickienė's 2015 study names Dilionis alone in Waterbury and places Rusikas in their later Baltimore attempt. Rusikas's Waterbury role therefore remains unresolved. No evidence supports merging this record with Roman Catholic St. Joseph or with today's Roman Catholic All Saints/Todos los Santos Parish.
gaps: No contemporary 1902 Waterbury notice, parish charter, deed, street address, dedicated church building, cemetery, sacramental register, membership count, formal Polish National Catholic Church affiliation, closure act, or exact end date has been found. The present Eastern Diocese PNCC directory establishes only that there is no current Waterbury parish in that directory; it cannot date the historical ending. Property and city-directory research is still needed to determine whether the organizers ever rented or owned a worship space. The current record should not assign a building fate or describe a living successor until that evidence is found.
